tracks.title: C++ foundations
tracks.description: Build reliable habits with values, decisions, loops, functions, and collections.

tracks.title: Real-world systems
tracks.description: Turn telemetry, events, caches, and networks into dependable algorithms.

tracks.title: Game development
tracks.description: Solve movement, scoring, scheduling, and frame-budget problems.

tracks.title: Compiler workshop
tracks.description: Explore scanners, build graphs, name versions, and bytecode machines.

challenges.title: Café receipt
challenges.summary: Turn a drink order into an exact bill.
challenges.story: The campus café is replacing handwritten receipts. Its terminal already reads the order; your function calculates the total in cents.

concepts.title: Whole-number money
concepts.body: Store prices in cents so this bill uses exact integer arithmetic. Multiplication combines the number of drinks with the price of one drink.

concepts.title: Return a result
concepts.body: A function returns one value to its caller. main prints that value and a newline.

challenges.prompt: Implement total_cost(quantity, unit_price). Every drink costs the same amount. Return the order total in cents.
challenges.input_format: Two integers: quantity and unit_price in cents.
challenges.output_format: One integer: the total price in cents.
constraints: Use long long for the product.
hints: A total is the price of one item repeated once for each item.
Use the * operator to multiply quantity and unit_price.
Return quantity * unit_price from total_cost.

challenges.title: Stockroom signal
challenges.summary: Decide when a shop needs to reorder.
challenges.story: A maker shop tracks spare components. A quantity strictly below its reorder threshold needs attention; an exact match is still ready.

concepts.title: A precise boundary
concepts.body: The requirement says strictly below. The < operator excludes equality, while <= includes it.

concepts.title: Two outcomes
concepts.body: An if statement chooses a path. Returning from the first path lets the following return handle every other case.

objectives: Translate a business rule into a comparison
challenges.prompt: Implement stock_status(quantity, threshold). Return REORDER when quantity is strictly less than threshold. Otherwise return READY.
challenges.input_format: Two integers: quantity and threshold.
hints: There are two outcomes, so an if statement is enough.
Equality belongs to READY. Compare with <, not <=.
If quantity < threshold return "REORDER"; otherwise return "READY".

challenges.title: Delivery odometer
challenges.summary: Add the legs of a delivery route.
challenges.story: A bicycle courier records each completed leg in meters. The dashboard needs the full distance, including routes with no completed legs.

concepts.title: An accumulator
concepts.body: Start a running total at zero. Visit each distance and add it once. The loop also behaves correctly for an empty vector.
concepts.code:
long long total = 0;
for (long long distance : distances) total += distance;

concepts.title: A wide sum
concepts.body: A collection of valid small inputs can produce a large sum. A long long accumulator avoids overflowing a 32-bit int.

objectives: Traverse a vector with a loop
challenges.prompt: Implement total_distance(distances). Return the sum of all recorded route legs.
challenges.input_format: An integer n, followed by n nonnegative distances in meters.
hints: Keep one running total as you visit each distance.
Initialize the total to zero before the loop.
Add every element to a long long total and return it after the loop.

challenges.title: Quest reward function
challenges.summary: Package a repeatable game rule in a function.
challenges.story: Your game awards a base reward plus one bonus for every completed objective. Other game systems will reuse this function, so keep input and output in main.

concepts.title: Separate a rule from I/O
concepts.body: A pure calculation takes arguments and returns a result. It can be tested without reading from cin or printing to cout.

concepts.title: Compose arithmetic
concepts.body: Calculate the total bonus with multiplication, then add the base reward. C++ evaluates multiplication before addition.

objectives: Keep calculation separate from console I/O
challenges.prompt: Implement quest_reward(base, completed, bonus). Return base plus completed times bonus.
challenges.input_format: Three integers: base reward, completed objective count, and bonus per objective.
hints: Find the bonus for all objectives first.
Multiply completed by bonus, then add base.
Return base + completed * bonus; main already prints the result.

challenges.title: Temperature watch
challenges.summary: Find the hottest sensor reading.
challenges.story: A cold-storage monitor records integer temperatures, including negative ones. Find the hottest observed reading so the operator can inspect it.

concepts.title: Initialize from real data
concepts.body: When all readings are negative, zero is not a valid starting maximum. Start with the first reading because the input is guaranteed nonempty.

concepts.title: Maintain an invariant
concepts.body: After visiting a reading, hottest should equal the largest value seen so far.

objectives: Find an extremum in one pass
challenges.prompt: Implement hottest_reading(readings). Return the largest temperature in the nonempty vector.
challenges.input_format: An integer n, followed by n integer temperatures.
hints: You only need to remember the largest value encountered so far.
Initialize that value with readings.front() so all-negative data works.
For every reading, replace hottest with max(hottest, reading), then return hottest.

challenges.title: Level-up ledger
challenges.summary: Convert accumulated XP into a player level.
challenges.story: Your first level begins at zero XP. Every full block of 100 XP adds one level; any remainder contributes to the next level.

concepts.title: Integer division
concepts.body: Dividing two nonnegative integers discards the fractional part. That counts completed 100-XP blocks.

concepts.title: An offset
concepts.body: Level numbers begin at one even though completed blocks begin at zero.

challenges.prompt: Implement player_level(xp). A player starts at level 1 and gains one level for each full 100 XP. Return their level.
challenges.input_format: One nonnegative integer xp.
hints: Count complete groups of 100 XP.
Use xp / 100; then account for the initial level.
Return xp / 100 + 1. Check both 99 XP and 100 XP.

challenges.title: Lexical signal counter
challenges.summary: Count selected characters in source text.
challenges.story: A tiny source-analysis tool marks each semicolon as a completed statement candidate. At this stage it simply counts characters; it does not parse C++ or ignore comments.

concepts.title: Characters and strings
concepts.body: A string is a sequence of characters. Single quotes describe a character such as ';'; double quotes describe a string.

concepts.title: Scope matters
concepts.body: A character counter is simpler than a parser. This exercise deliberately counts every semicolon, wherever it appears.

challenges.prompt: Implement count_semicolons(source). Return the number of semicolon characters in the input line. Count every semicolon, including repeated ones.
challenges.input_format: One line of text, which may be empty or contain spaces.
hints: Visit each character and test whether it is a semicolon.
Start a count at zero and increment only on character == ';'.
Use a range-based for loop over source, then return the count.

challenges.title: Latency snapshot
challenges.summary: Report an integer average for service timing.
challenges.story: A local service records request durations in microseconds. Its status panel displays the average rounded down, using exact integer arithmetic.

concepts.title: Sum before dividing
concepts.body: Divide the final total once. Dividing individual values first loses information and can change the answer.

concepts.title: Integer mean
concepts.body: For nonnegative values, integer division rounds the mean down. The input is nonempty so the divisor is never zero.

challenges.prompt: Implement average_latency(durations). Return the floor of the average duration.
challenges.input_format: An integer n, followed by n durations in microseconds.
challenges.output_format: One integer: the average rounded down.
hints: Compute one total for all durations.
Divide that total by durations.size(), once.
Keep total as long long and use integer division for the required rounding.

challenges.title: Tile navigator
challenges.summary: Measure movement on a square game board.
challenges.story: A turn-based character can move one tile up, down, left, or right. The board has no obstacles, so calculate the minimum moves between two coordinates.

concepts.title: Independent axes
concepts.body: Horizontal and vertical displacement must both be covered. A shortest route never wastes movement reversing direction.

concepts.title: Absolute differences
concepts.body: A distance is nonnegative regardless of coordinate order. Use the magnitude of each coordinate difference.
concepts.code: long long dx = x1 > x2 ? x1 - x2 : x2 - x1;

challenges.prompt: Implement tile_distance(x1, y1, x2, y2). Return the shortest four-direction move count on an obstacle-free integer grid.
challenges.input_format: Four integers: x1 y1 x2 y2.
constraints: A move changes exactly one coordinate by 1.
hints: Count the necessary horizontal and vertical moves separately.
Take the absolute difference for x and the absolute difference for y.
Add those differences. Use long long because the total can exceed 32-bit int.

challenges.title: Duplicate reservations
challenges.summary: Count seats after repeated booking events.
challenges.story: A community theater receives booking events that may be retried. Repeated events for the same seat must consume that seat only once.

concepts.title: A set stores membership
concepts.body: A set represents distinct values. Inserting an existing seat does not add a second copy.

concepts.title: Idempotent events
concepts.body: An operation is idempotent when applying it repeatedly has the same result as applying it once. Distinct-seat counting provides that behavior here.

objectives: Use a set to remove duplicates
challenges.prompt: Implement available_seats(capacity, bookings). Every booking refers to a valid seat. Return capacity minus the number of distinct booked seats.
challenges.input_format: Integers capacity and m, followed by m seat numbers.
hints: The number of events can be larger than the number of occupied seats.
Insert each seat into a set so retries do not increase occupancy.
Subtract the set size from capacity.

challenges.title: Burst detector
challenges.summary: Find the busiest fixed-length sensor window.
challenges.story: A monitoring service groups a stream into consecutive windows. Find the largest total in any window of exactly k readings, including streams whose readings are all negative.

concepts.title: Reuse neighboring work
concepts.body: Adjacent windows share k − 1 elements. Subtract the departing value and add the arriving value instead of summing from scratch.

concepts.title: State and boundaries
concepts.body: Build the first full window before updating the best result. This handles k = n and all-negative streams.

objectives: Handle the first window and negative totals
challenges.prompt: Implement max_window_sum(readings, k). Return the largest sum of exactly k consecutive readings.
challenges.input_format: Integers n and k, followed by n signed readings.
challenges.output_format: One integer: the maximum window sum.
hints: Sum the first k readings to establish the first valid window.
When shifting right, remove readings[i-k] and add readings[i].
Initialize best to the first window sum, then update best after every shift.

challenges.title: Warehouse merge
challenges.summary: Combine stock adjustments and print a stable report.
challenges.story: Two warehouse feeds have been concatenated. Item identifiers can appear many times, including negative adjustments. Produce one total per item in alphabetical order.

concepts.title: Map keys to totals
concepts.body: A map associates an item name with an accumulated quantity. operator[] creates a zero-initialized total for a new key.

concepts.title: Deterministic iteration
concepts.body: std::map visits keys in sorted order. This gives a stable report without a separate sorting pass.

challenges.prompt: Implement merge_inventory(records). Return a map from each item name to the sum of its adjustments. Keep entries whose final total is zero. main prints the map in ascending name order.
challenges.input_format: An integer n, followed by n lines containing item_name and signed adjustment.
challenges.output_format: One line per distinct item: item_name total. Print nothing when n is zero.
hints: Use an item name as a key and its accumulated stock as the value.
A map<string, long long> both aggregates quantities and orders names.
For each record, execute totals[item] += adjustment. Return totals without removing zero entries.

challenges.title: Incident streak
challenges.summary: Find the longest uninterrupted repeated status.
challenges.story: A service log stores status codes in arrival order. The operations team wants the longest consecutive run of one code, even when the code itself is zero.

concepts.title: Consecutive is different from frequent
concepts.body: Only adjacent equal values belong to the same run. A later appearance after another code begins a new run.

concepts.title: Two counters
concepts.body: Track the current run length and the largest completed or current run. Reset the current length to one when the code changes.

challenges.prompt: Implement longest_run(codes). Return the length of the longest contiguous run of equal codes. Return zero for an empty log.
challenges.input_format: An integer n, followed by n status codes.
hints: Remember the run ending at the current position, not just a code frequency.
Equal to the previous code means extend the run; otherwise start at one.
Update best every iteration, and initialize both counters to zero for an empty vector.

challenges.title: Packet parity
challenges.summary: Fold packet bytes into an XOR checksum.
challenges.story: A device protocol includes a simple XOR checksum. It helps detect some transmission errors, but is not a cryptographic integrity check. Recreate the protocol exactly.

concepts.title: Bitwise XOR
concepts.body: The ^ operator combines individual bits. Equal bits produce zero and different bits produce one. Applying the same value twice cancels it.

concepts.title: Identity element
concepts.body: XOR with zero leaves a value unchanged, so zero is the correct initial checksum and the result for an empty packet.

challenges.prompt: Implement packet_checksum(bytes). XOR all byte values and return the result as a decimal integer.
challenges.input_format: An integer n, followed by n decimal byte values.
hints: Combine values with ^, which is XOR in C++; it is not exponentiation.
Start at zero and XOR each byte into the accumulator.
Return the accumulator. Two identical bytes cancel each other.

challenges.title: Expression scanner
challenges.summary: Split arithmetic source into lexical tokens.
challenges.story: Before a compiler builds a syntax tree, its scanner groups characters into tokens. Build a tiny scanner for nonnegative decimal integers and arithmetic punctuation.

concepts.title: Maximal digit runs
concepts.body: A number token consumes every consecutive digit. The source text 120 contains one number token, not three.

concepts.title: A scanner advances
concepts.body: At each position, skip whitespace, scan a full number, or emit one punctuation character. Each branch must advance the index.

challenges.prompt: Implement scan_tokens(source). Ignore spaces. A maximal run of digits is one token; each +, -, *, /, (, or ) is a separate token. Do not evaluate the expression. main prints the token count and then tokens joined by single spaces.
challenges.input_format: One line containing digits, spaces, and the punctuation + - * / ( ). The line may be empty.
challenges.output_format: First line: token count. Second line: tokens separated by single spaces; an empty token list produces an empty second line.
constraints: Preserve number spelling, including leading zeroes.
hints: Use an index to walk the string and skip spaces.
When a digit starts a token, advance until the next character is not a digit.
Save that digit substring; otherwise emit a one-character punctuation token and advance once.

challenges.title: Leaderboard cut
challenges.summary: Select top scores without losing ties.
challenges.story: A tournament display has room for k score entries. Repeated scores belong to different players and must remain present. Show the selected entries in descending order.

concepts.title: Ordering with a comparator
concepts.body: std::sort accepts a comparison that places larger values first. Equal scores stay as distinct entries.

concepts.title: Copy and resize
concepts.body: Passing the vector by value gives the function a local copy it may sort. Resizing after sorting selects the first k values.

challenges.prompt: Implement top_scores(scores, k). Return the k largest scores in descending order, preserving duplicates.
challenges.input_format: Integers n and k, followed by n signed scores.
challenges.output_format: The k selected scores on one line separated by single spaces. Print an empty line when k is zero.
hints: A descending sort places the desired entries at the beginning.
Do not put scores in a set: that would remove tied entries.
Sort with greater<long long>(), then resize the vector to k.

challenges.title: Request cache
challenges.summary: Simulate a least-recently-used cache.
challenges.story: An API gateway caches recently requested assets. A hit refreshes an asset; a miss loads it and may evict the least recently used asset. Measure hits and misses for a request trace.

concepts.title: Two structures, one invariant
concepts.body: A list stores recency from newest to oldest. A hash map points each cached key to its list iterator. Every cached key must appear exactly once in each structure.

concepts.title: Refresh without a search
concepts.body: list::splice moves an existing node without invalidating its iterator. New keys go at the front; eviction removes the back.

objectives: Maintain a consistent list and hash index
challenges.prompt: Implement cache_counts(capacity, requests). The cache starts empty. A cached request is a hit and becomes most recent. Otherwise count a miss, insert it as most recent, and evict the least recent key if capacity is exceeded. Return {hits, misses}.
challenges.input_format: Integers capacity and n, followed by n request keys.
hints: You need membership lookup plus the order of recent use; one queue alone makes hit refresh expensive.
Use unordered_map<int, list<int>::iterator> with the most recent list entry at the front.
On a hit splice its node to the front. On a miss insert at the front and erase the back key from both structures if over capacity.

challenges.title: Rescue route
challenges.summary: Find a shortest route through a blocked game map.
challenges.story: A rescue unit must reach an exit using four-direction movement. All moves cost one turn, and walls cannot be crossed. Report the fewest turns or signal that rescue is impossible.

concepts.title: Breadth-first layers
concepts.body: A FIFO queue visits reachable cells in increasing distance when every move has equal cost. The first distance assigned to a cell is therefore shortest.

concepts.title: Visit when enqueuing
concepts.body: Mark a cell as visited as soon as you add it to the queue. That prevents many frontier cells from enqueueing it repeatedly.

challenges.prompt: Implement rescue_distance(grid). Find the minimum number of up, down, left, or right moves from S to E. Return -1 if no route exists. Each grid contains exactly one S and one E.
challenges.input_format: Integers rows and columns, followed by rows strings containing ., #, S, or E.
challenges.output_format: One integer: shortest move count, or -1.
constraints: Every row has exactly columns characters.
hints: Every move has the same cost, so use BFS from S.
Store distance -1 for unseen cells and set distance before pushing a neighbor into the queue.
Check four neighbors, rejecting out-of-bounds cells and walls. Return the distance when E leaves the queue, or -1 if the queue empties.

challenges.title: Build graph
challenges.summary: Schedule compiler targets in dependency order.
challenges.story: A build tool must compile dependencies before their consumers. When several targets are ready, it picks the smallest identifier to keep logs reproducible. Cycles make the build impossible.

concepts.title: Incoming dependencies
concepts.body: The indegree of a target counts prerequisites still unfinished. A zero-indegree target is ready to build.

concepts.title: Deterministic Kahn algorithm
concepts.body: Use a min-priority queue for ready targets. Removing a target decrements each consumer indegree. If fewer than n targets are emitted, a cycle remains.

challenges.prompt: Implement build_order(n, edges). Each pair u v means target u must be built before v. Return the lexicographically smallest valid target order. Return an empty vector if a cycle prevents a full order. main prints CYCLE for that result.
challenges.input_format: Integers n and m, followed by m lines u v.
challenges.output_format: All n target identifiers in build order, separated by spaces, or CYCLE.
constraints: Edges may repeat; self-dependencies form a cycle.
hints: Count the prerequisites of each node and start with nodes that have none.
Use a min-heap so every step chooses the smallest currently ready target.
After removing a target, decrement its consumers. If the emitted order has fewer than n nodes, return an empty vector for a cycle.

challenges.title: Arena event scheduler
challenges.summary: Fit the most events on a single game server.
challenges.story: A tournament server can host only one event at a time. An event ending at time t can be followed immediately by another starting at t. Choose the largest number of compatible events.

concepts.title: Greedy choice
concepts.body: Selecting the available event that finishes earliest leaves at least as much room for later events as selecting a later-finishing alternative.

concepts.title: Half-open intervals
concepts.body: Treat an event as [start, end). Two events are compatible when the later start is greater than or equal to the previous end.

challenges.prompt: Implement max_events(events). Each pair is {start, end} with start < end. Return the maximum number of non-overlapping events. Events that touch at an endpoint do not overlap.
challenges.input_format: An integer n, followed by n lines start end.
challenges.output_format: One integer: maximum compatible event count.
hints: Choosing the shortest duration is not always optimal. Consider which choice frees the server earliest.
Sort events by increasing end time.
Keep the next available time; accept an event when start >= available, then set available = end.

challenges.title: SSA name ledger
challenges.summary: Give each straight-line assignment a unique name.
challenges.story: A toy compiler prepares straight-line assignments for later analysis. Each write gets a fresh version; each variable read refers to the latest earlier version. This is a name-renaming exercise, not a complete LLVM or control-flow SSA implementation.

concepts.title: Definitions and uses
concepts.body: Process the right-hand side before assigning a new version to the left-hand side. In x = x, the right x must refer to the older definition.

concepts.title: Initial versions
concepts.body: A variable read before any assignment refers to version 0. A first assignment creates version 1. Integer literals pass through unchanged.

objectives: Separate definition order from use lookup
Understand the limits of straight-line SSA
challenges.prompt: Implement rename_assignments(assignments). Each pair means lhs = rhs. A variable name contains lowercase letters only. rhs is either a variable name or a nonnegative integer literal. Rewrite variables as name.version; reads use the latest previous version or 0, and each write increments its lhs version. Return formatted lines exactly as lhs.version = rhs.
challenges.input_format: An integer n, followed by n lines lhs rhs.
challenges.output_format: One rewritten assignment per line, with one space on each side of =.
constraints: Variable names contain 1 to 20 lowercase letters.
Integer literals contain 1 to 20 digits; preserve their spelling.
There are no branches or phi nodes in this exercise.
hints: Maintain a map from each variable name to its latest assigned version.
Resolve rhs using the current map before incrementing lhs; otherwise x = x reads its own new version.
Leave numeric rhs unchanged, append the current version to variable rhs, then increment lhs and format the assignment.

tests.input:
4
x 5
y x
x y
z x

challenges.title: Bytecode stack machine
challenges.summary: Execute a tiny arithmetic instruction stream.
challenges.story: A game scripting runtime uses stack bytecode. Implement PUSH, ADD, SUB, and MUL so scripted calculations run in their original operand order. The provided programs are valid.

concepts.title: Stack operands
concepts.body: PUSH adds a value. A binary instruction removes rhs first and then lhs. It pushes the result of lhs op rhs. This ordering matters for subtraction.

concepts.title: A compact virtual machine
concepts.body: The program is a sequence of named operations. Dispatch each operation and update explicit machine state; no dynamic code evaluation is required.

challenges.prompt: Implement execute_bytecode(program). PUSH has its integer argument in the pair; ADD, SUB, and MUL ignore that field. Run all instructions and return the sole final stack value.
challenges.input_format: An integer n, followed by n instructions. Each instruction is PUSH value, ADD, SUB, or MUL.
challenges.output_format: One integer: the final stack result.
constraints: All programs have enough operands and finish with exactly one value.
Every input and intermediate result fits signed 64-bit long long.
hints: Use vector<long long> as a stack, with push_back, back, and pop_back.
For binary operations, the first popped value is rhs and the next is lhs.
Push lhs + rhs, lhs - rhs, or lhs * rhs. Return the last value after the full program.

tests.input:
7
PUSH 4
PUSH 3
ADD
PUSH 2
PUSH 1
SUB
MUL

challenges.title: Network route planner
challenges.summary: Find a minimum-cost directed network route.
challenges.story: A service mesh advertises nonnegative link delays. Choose the lowest total delay from a source to a destination. Links are directed and a destination may be unreachable.

concepts.title: Dijkstra and nonnegative weights
concepts.body: A min-priority queue processes the smallest tentative distance. Nonnegative edge weights make finalizing distances in this order valid.

concepts.title: Lazy queue entries
concepts.body: When a better distance is found, push a new entry. Older entries can remain in the queue; skip them when their stored distance differs from the current best.

objectives: Use wide distances and unreachable sentinels
challenges.prompt: Implement shortest_delay(n, edges, source, target). Each edge is {from, to, weight}. Return the minimum summed weight of a directed route, or -1 if no route exists. A source equal to the target has distance zero.
challenges.input_format: Integers n, m, source, target, followed by m lines from to weight.
constraints: Parallel edges and zero-weight edges are allowed.
hints: A FIFO BFS queue is insufficient because link weights differ. Use a min-priority queue of {distance, node}.
Relax an edge only when cost + weight improves the stored distance, then push the improved entry.
Skip stale entries. Start source at zero, all others at a large sentinel, and return -1 if target is never reached.

challenges.title: Frame budget optimizer
challenges.summary: Choose render effects within a strict time budget.
challenges.story: A game can enable optional visual effects for the next frame. Every effect has an integer cost and a quality value. Each effect may be enabled once; maximize quality without exceeding the frame budget.

concepts.title: A dynamic-programming state
concepts.body: dp[b] stores the greatest quality obtainable using processed effects with total cost at most b. Initially every budget achieves quality zero by choosing nothing.

concepts.title: Iterate budgets backward
concepts.body: For a 0/1 choice, update budgets from high to low so the current effect cannot be reused in the same iteration. Forward updates would solve a different, repeatable-item problem.
concepts.code:
for (int b = budget; b >= cost; --b)
    dp[b] = max(dp[b], dp[b - cost] + quality);

objectives: Define and implement a one-dimensional DP
challenges.prompt: Implement best_quality(budget, effects). Each pair is {cost, quality}. Choose any subset, using each effect at most once. Return the maximum total quality with total cost no greater than budget.
challenges.input_format: Integers n and budget, followed by n lines cost quality.
hints: Represent the best quality for each allowed budget from zero through budget.
For an effect, compare skipping it with adding its quality to the best result at b - cost.
Process b downward from budget to cost; ascending order would allow taking the same effect repeatedly.
